classification.difficultyReason: Completes the square for two starting curves, then applies the stated axis reflections, distinguishing replacement of x by -x from negation of the entire expression.

content.prompt: Written in standard form, the equations of two of the parabolas below are $y=x^2+12x+27$ and $y=x^2+12x+36$. The other parabolas are obtained from one of these upon reflection in the $x$- and $y$-axes. Find the equations of all eight parabolas in turning point form.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, graph below the stem in the upper right column
spec.description: Eight unshaded equation-driven parabolas on shared unticked axes, symmetric in both axes. Each side has two vertices on the x-axis, one above it and one below it. Source blue curves and grey axes use house black because their hues convey no mathematical distinction.
spec.mathematics: For each h in {-6,6}, the four curves are y=(x-h)^2, y=-(x-h)^2, y=(x-h)^2-9 and y=-(x-h)^2+9. Preserve their intersections and relative vertices without printing numerical labels.
spec.answerVisibility: All eight curves and x/y axis labels are permanent question givens. Equations, numerical ticks and vertex coordinates are not printed in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+12x+27\\y&=(x^2+12x+36)-36+27\\y&=(x+6)^2-9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+12x+36\\y&=(x+6)^2\end{align*}$$
Reflection in the $y$-axis replaces $x$ by $-x$. Reflection in the $x$-axis negates the whole expression. Reflecting in both axes does both.

From $y=(x+6)^2-9$, the four equations are
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(x+6)^2-9\\y&=(x-6)^2-9\\y&=-(x+6)^2+9\\y&=-(x-6)^2+9.\end{aligned}$$
From $y=(x+6)^2$, the four equations are
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(x+6)^2\\y&=(x-6)^2\\y&=-(x+6)^2\\y&=-(x-6)^2.\end{aligned}$$
